title: Move "OS setup" files to their own subfolder in \tools
description:
Organize all of the OS setup script files into their own subfolder in \tools
Adjust calling scripts and documentation accordingly.

notes.body: This is in an effort to help cleanup the \tools directory

@johnthacker - 7bf71c0b3a5aa4122b2eed154119d3d59f5bc355 changed the Alpine script from bash to ash, however the script itself was never checked by shellcheck.  I thought that was a mistake and tried to "fix the glitch" as part of this MR.  Should the fix be to remove the "&" (as the warning suggests) or because the script is ash, it shouldn't be handled by shellcheck?
I think we probably want to leave the execute bit set on all of the setup scripts, seems like it got cleared when moving them.
Nice catch, I'll blame Windows for that.  Fixed.

> Should the fix be to remove the "&" (as the warning suggests

I think the fix is to replace `&> /dev/null` with `> /dev/null 2>&1`, assuming that `dash` in Alpine doesn't support that Bashism. It doesn't hurt to replace it even if supported, it's just more verbose.

I'm not sure how many people use these scripts in automation pipelines, but in our case we'll have to update most of our Dockerfiles at https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/-/tree/master/development.
I put an MR in place to update the Dockerfiles (https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark-containers/-/merge_requests/99).  What should the approval steps be for it all?
I went ahead and approved it; we just need to remember to merge after this MR.
